title: burst-window-coalescence-leads-to-cross-key-burst-amplification-and-metering-skew
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:

Production observed that a small fraction of API keys receive a transient 3-5x burst of allow windows during shard rebalances and planned policy hot-reloads. The symptom is an apparent sudden burst of traffic that bypasses per-key burst caps and causes downstream billing/metering spikes and SLO breaches for affected tenants.

Scope / Where it happens:
- Affects the rate engine path that performs window coalescence (merge adjacent short windows for efficiency) during policy refresh and shard lease handoffs.
- Reproducible on multi-tenant edge shards (shard-group-2/3) when concurrent policy hot-reloads and route alias updates happen.
- Observed in hosted runtime and Dedicated staging; not yet seen in Private on-prem controlled clusters.

Observed impact:
- Transient allowance amplification (customers seeing 3-5x allowed requests for ~30-90s) despite configured burst budgets.
- Metering duplication on the ingestion side in some failover paths (double-count seen in aggregated usage snapshots).
- Several customers triggered downstream rate-limit alarms and one high-usage account moved into an overage window.

Hypothesis / Root cause (current):
- During policy refresh, the window coalescer merges near-edge windows across two internal namespaces (per-key and per-org) using a shared transient allocator. Under concurrent updates the allocator can hand out a single merged window token that is incorrectly applied to multiple logical buckets (per-key + per-route) because the merge key generation omitted the shard-lease epoch in one code path. This creates an overlapping allowance that is consumed once per logical path, effectively amplifying the original budget.

Proposed fixes (short + long):
1) Short-term mitigation (hotfix): disable coalescence for co-tenant window types and enable strict namespace-scoped merge keys. Deployment: runtime-2.4.1-hotfix. Rollout plan: staged to edge shards; monitor Grafana permit/allow ratio.
2) Medium-term: add epoch-aware merge key and atomic multi-bucket reservation semantics in the coalescer to prevent accidental aliasing across logical buckets. Add unit tests that simulate concurrent policy hot-reload + shard handoff.
3) Long-term: extend system tests to include controlled policy churn with synthetic traffic to exercise coalescence paths and ensure metering invariants.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reproducer rate reduced to zero in staged clusters under the same workload profile.
- No duplicate metering events for the same logical request in the aggregation pipeline.
- Canaryed hotfix shows normalized per-key burst counts and no customer-impacting overages for 72 hours.

Rollback plan:
- If hotfix increases latency or causes new rejects, revert coalescence toggle and fall back to pre-2.4 coalescer behavior. Maintain route-level rate limit enforcement to avoid silent allows.

Telemetry and dashboards referenced:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd/rate-engine-permits?orgId=1 (permit/allow ratio, per-shard breakdown)
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/efgh/metering-duplicates (duplicate-meter event counts)

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence writeup: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/Window+Coalescence+Bug+Postmortem
- Reproducer script (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcReproExample
- GitHub hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-engine/pull/1823
- GitHub unit test PR (work-in-progress): https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-engine/pull/1830

Notes:
- This is related to earlier findings in ENG-314271 but manifests differently (coalescer allocator vs. shard epoch desync).
- Notify customer success and on-call billing team prior to canary release.
